facts.claim: Within-person fluctuations in friendship quality predicted within-person fluctuations in self-esteem, and this association was stronger for singles than for partnered people.
facts.quote: Multilevel modeling revealed that within-person fluctuations in friendship quality predicted within-person fluctuations in self-esteem, and this association was stronger for singles than for partnered people.

facts.claim: Singles invested more in their friendships than partnered people, and greater friendship investment predicted greater friendship quality and self-esteem later on.
facts.quote: A cross-sectional mediation analysis also revealed that singles invested more in their friendships than partnered people, and greater friendship investment predicted greater friendship quality and self-esteem later on.

facts.claim: The number of interworldview friendships in the first year on campus is positively associated with pluralism orientation.
facts.quote: Results revealed that, holding constant other predictors, the number of interworldview friendships in the first year on campus is positively associated with pluralism orientation.

facts.claim: Hours together was associated with closer friendships.
facts.quote: Hours together was associated with closer friendships.

facts.claim: Time spent engaging in leisure activities also predicted closeness.
facts.quote: Time spent engaging in leisure activities also predicted closeness.

research.angle: Friendship closeness is associated with the amount of time spent together, shared leisure activities, and specific types of everyday talk.
research.verdict: The evidence shows that time spent together and engagement in activities are associated with closer friendships and higher self-esteem, particularly for single individuals.
research.caveat: The studies primarily show associations rather than proving that spending time together is the direct cause of friendship closeness.
